strongest_candidate.question: Assuming Medtronic, Stryker, and Penumbra ALL succeed with next-generation thrombectomy devices, what failure remains?
strongest_candidate.answer: 20% of clots are RECALCITRANT — they fail to recanalize or require multiple passes. This is a PHYSICAL LIMITATION of mechanical retrieval: some clots are too hard, too sticky, or too fragmented for stent retrievers or aspiration.
strongest_candidate.why_this_is_different_from_IIH_VSS: IIH/VSS: device works but physiology changes over time. Stroke: device architecture CANNOT address certain clot types — the failure is in the MECHANISM, not the ADAPTATION.
strongest_candidate.next_campaign_question: What new technical primitive could address recalcitrant clots that mechanical thrombectomy cannot?

ce_gate_preliminary_check.CE-012: Recalcitrant clot removal is NOT 'existing measurement + AI' — it requires a new PHYSICAL mechanism, not analysis of existing data
ce_gate_preliminary_check.CE-013: Clot composition (fibrin-rich, calcified, cholesterol-rich) is causally INDEPENDENT of the retrieval device — it's a property of the clot, not a downstream consequence of the device
ce_gate_preliminary_check.CE-014: Must search using patent vocabulary (thrombectomy, embolectomy, clot retrieval, recanalization) not our terminology
ce_gate_preliminary_check.CE-015: Must calculate physical authority before proposing mechanism (can the proposed approach actually remove a hard clot?)
